sources.supports: getReports validates the project identifier with validateId and places it as the only path segment of get_reports; getCrossProjectReports takes no argument and requests get_cross_project_reports. runReport and runCrossProjectReport validate the template identifier the same way and place it as the only path segment of run_report and run_cross_project_report, requesting with bypassCache true and retry rateLimitOnly. Their comments record that each call generates a new report and the template may email it, so the cache and in-flight coalescing are bypassed and every explicit call executes once, and that only a 429 is retried because the rate limiter rejects before execution, so nothing was generated.

ReportSchema requires id and name and admits a nullish description and the nullish notify_user, notify_link, notify_link_recipients, notify_attachment, notify_attachment_recipients, notify_attachment_html_format and notify_attachment_pdf_format fields, beside a nullish is_shared. CrossProjectReportSchema also requires project_ids, include_open_runs_and_plans, include_completed_runs_and_plans and report_timeframe, and its comment records that the Summary-only and User Workload-only selections stay optional because TestRail omits them from the other family, and that included_statuses admits both a list and the comma-separated string of the wire example. ReportResultSchema requires report_url and admits nullish report_html, report_pdf and user_report_url, the last kept only for older revisions. Every object is passthrough, so unmodelled keys survive parsing.

Only reports created with "Create this report: On-demand via the API" checked are accessible to the API; they appear under API Templates and are visible and executable through these endpoints, and the setting cannot be changed once a report is saved. A report may not be available immediately after being run, and the delay varies, especially on TestRail Server. get_reports/{project_id} takes a required project_id and returns an array of API-available single-project reports; it answers 400 for an invalid or unknown project and 403 for no access to the project. run_report/{report_template_id} requires TestRail 5.7 or later, executes the report and returns report_url, report_html and report_pdf; it answers 400 for an invalid report template ID and 403 for no access to the project. get_cross_project_reports takes no input parameter and returns the API-available cross-project reports the user has access to, for Enterprise license plans only; its 403 is described as "TestRail Enterprise only. Access denied. User role does not grant access." run_cross_project_report/{report_template_id} is likewise Enterprise only and returns the same three URLs, with the same 400 and 403. The notify_* fields describe whether the author is notified once the report has been executed, whether links or attachments are emailed, and to whom.

input_policy.notes: The endpoint takes nothing: TestRail documents no input parameter and the driver sends none, so every field is refused. The templates it returns span projects, so a caller naming a project is refused rather than served the unnarrowed list as if it had been filtered.

outer_result.notes: The array of templates is returned as the driver received it. The two report families carry different optional fields, Summary-only milestones on one and User Workload-only users, times and sorting on the other, and neither is filled in for the other. Entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Call the driver with no arguments at all, and send no path segment, query or body.
